clue.text: Is quoted backwards about being non-specifically religious

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the clue's opening word
backwards tells us the word for quoted is read from end to start

parts.note: something quoted has been cited
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's words are quoted in reverse while discussing vague religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns the synonym for quoted end to end, giving DETIC, and 'about' then has it go round the clue's opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deist believes in a creator God without the doctrines of any particular faith, so deistic belief is religion of a non-specific kind.

clue.text: Dead river, or the merest trickle

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, north-west England

explanation.surface: A dried-up river, reduced to almost nothing flowing along it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dribble is a thin, feeble flow of liquid, the smallest of trickles.

clue.text: Modify or pass on disease across line

indicators.note: across means the disease word stretches over the letter for line, holding it inside

parts.note: to infect someone is to pass a disease on to them

explanation.surface: A request to alter, or else spread, an illness along a line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect a word is to change its form, as for tense or number; more broadly, to vary or alter.

clue.text: Wound up finding one score halved and another gutted

parts.note: a score is twenty, and half of that is ten
another score, emptied of its middle, leaves its first and last letters S and E

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious after seeing one result cut in half and another wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: The scores look like match results; the first is the number twenty and the second is the word score itself with its insides removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wound up is nervous and on edge, which is what being tense means.

clue.text: Old garment adopted by government leader after call from Moss, say

indicators.note: after places the wrapped garment behind the word for call

parts.note: to call out is to cry

indicators.note: adopted by means the garment is taken in by the leader's letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: PM is short for Prime Minister, the leader of a government
the toga was the garment of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister dons a toga after hearing a cry from a person called Moss.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss looks like a surname, but it is the plant, an example of the class defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogam is a plant reproducing by spores rather than seeds, and mosses are a classic example.

clue.text: Battered hat with blemish at a funny angle

indicators.note: a battered hat is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a wart is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A dented hat and a skin flaw make someone look askew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' rearranges HAT to give ATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across or crosswise, lying slantwise rather than straight.

clue.text: Honour accorded to a king supplies cautionary signal

parts.note: the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Granting an honour to a monarch serves as a warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the traffic-light colour warning drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Like running water, perhaps, left by snake as a gesture of friendship?

parts.note: taps supplying running water are marked H and C, hot and cold
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A friendly gesture is compared to flowing water and a serpent left nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Running water comes hot and cold, written H AND C on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A handclasp, gripping another's hand, is a common sign of friendship or greeting.

clue.text: American bum, say, with top-notch African weapon

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside
say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

explanation.surface: An American layabout teams up with a first-class spear from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, the first-class rating, is written with the letter I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by peoples of southern Africa.

clue.text: Grass production reportedly preserved spirit

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: preserved food may be tinned, and rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Seems to describe cannabis being grown, with alcohol kept in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is not the drug but Günter Grass, the German novelist; tinned rum, said quickly, sounds like the novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Drum is the best-known novel by Günter Grass, so it is literally a Grass production.

clue.text: Imaginarily innocent period?

definitions.meaning: the earliest stage of life, a time of innocence

explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is early childhood, the innocent period of life; split in two, it says in fancy, meaning imaginarily.

clue.text: Kingsley's playing for sacerdotal approbation

parts.note: Ben Kingsley is the actor, and 's stands for is
something playing, like a film, is on

explanation.surface: Seems to be about the actor Kingsley's performance and a priestly seal of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis is the obvious first thought, but it is Sir Ben Kingsley, the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is a blessing, such as a priest gives in approval.

clue.text: Ceremonial soldier's electronic exploit in the drink

indicators.note: in places these letters within the word for the drink

parts.note: beer is the drink in question
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
an exploit is a feat, a bold deed

explanation.surface: A Tower guard performs some e-feat while sitting in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders guarding the Tower of London in Tudor ceremonial uniform.

clue.text: Not initially sad about Cuban export

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
not initially means the opening letter of the word for sad is dropped

parts.note: something tragic is sad

explanation.surface: Someone not at first gloomy about a product from Havana.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAGIC loses its first letter to give RAGIC, which 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is famous for its hand-rolled cigars, among its best-known exports.

clue.text: Bar's to bar drunken poets

indicators.note: drunken poets reel about, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A legal ban on poets who have had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bar is the legal profession: ESTOP is a lawyer's word meaning to bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to preclude a party from asserting something, so it is the Bar's verb for barring.

clue.text: Tripe eater dropping a faulty 3

indicators.note: faulty means the letters are wrongly put together and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram's pool
the a that is left out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone who eats offal makes a grammatical error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes A from TRIPE EATER and 'faulty' rearranges the rest; 3 is a cross-reference to 3-down, TENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The preterite is the simple past, one grammatical tense, the answer to 3-down.

clue.text: Flower absorbing source of metallic element

indicators.note: absorbing means the flower takes the letter into itself

parts.note: the geranium is a garden flower

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of metallic

explanation.surface: A plant soaking up a metal from its roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a grey metalloid chemical element, number 32, used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Deny getting help to go up in estimation

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for estimation

parts.note: repute is the estimation in which one is held

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means being read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Disowning someone while needing their support to improve your standing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to go up' reads the help word from bottom to top, giving DIA, and 'in' tucks that into the word for estimation.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or disown, refusing to accept something as true; to deny it.

clue.text: Meet incongruously, in reversed roles, with local guide

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the reversed word
reversed means the word for roles is written backwards

parts.note: an actor's roles are parts

indicators.note: incongruously means oddly arranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Meeting oddly with roles swapped, using a guide to the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incongruously' turns MEET into EETM, which goes 'in' STRAP, the word PARTS that 'reversed' turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A street map is a plan of the roads of a town, a guide to the locality.

clue.text: Antichristian breed embraced by Spanish saint

indicators.note: embraced by means the breed goes inside the saint's title

parts.note: San is the Spanish word for Saint, as in San Diego
a breed is a race or stock

explanation.surface: A hostile lineage is hugged by a holy man from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saracens were the Muslim opponents of the Christian crusaders, so in medieval eyes the enemies of Christianity.

clue.text: Gun turned on North American star

indicators.note: turned means the word for gun is read backwards

parts.note: the Luger is a German pistol
US, the United States, stands for North American

explanation.surface: A weapon is pointed at an American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes REGUL out of LUGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulus is the brightest star in the constellation Leo.

clue.text: Apple, or purveyor thereof to teacher?

definitions.meaning: the apple of the eye is the dark central opening of the eye
a schoolchild traditionally brings an apple for the teacher

explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is both the dark centre of the eye, once called its apple, and a schoolchild who might hand a teacher an apple.

clue.text: The support one received as an innovator

indicators.note: received means the support takes the number in, holding it inside

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A backer takes someone in and treats them as a trailblazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is someone first to develop a new idea or method, an innovator.

clue.text: Woman following deduction cracks solution

indicators.note: cracks means the inserted word breaks into the solution word and sits inside it

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution
a nett amount is what remains after deductions

explanation.surface: Seems to be a detective whose reasoning breaks a case open.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests detective work, but deduction is subtraction, giving the nett figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynette is a woman's name; Lynette is also a lady in the Arthurian romances.

clue.text: Anomalous accent in which first letter's dropped

indicators.note: first letter's dropped means the opening letter of the accent word is removed

parts.note: a brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.surface: An odd way of speaking that swallows the initial sound of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue as an adjective means abnormal or out of line, as in a rogue wave or rogue result.

clue.text: I had earmarked the lady, as a Londoner might say, for cover

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops initial h, so the phrase is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: I'd her down, meaning I had her noted, with the Cockney dropped h

explanation.surface: A Cockney admits having singled out a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: To have someone down for something is to earmark them; a Cockney says 'I'd 'er down'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with down, a cover for a bed.

clue.text: Spain's opening fixture

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: A Spanish football club's first match of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Spain's opening looks like its first letter S; it is Spain's code E, with 's as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixture is a scheduled sporting event.

clue.text: Furious at being born in mid-assault

indicators.note: in mid means the letter goes into the middle of the assault word

parts.note: a raid is a sudden assault
b is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone enraged at being born in the middle of an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means furiously violent or fanatical, as well as having rabies.

clue.text: Suddenly meet dog eating duck's head

indicators.note: eating means the dog takes the letter inside itself

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

indicators.note: head means the first letter of duck

explanation.surface: A dog crashes into another animal while gobbling a duck's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To collide is to crash into something, to meet with sudden violent impact.

clue.text: Time to ban recycled music in shops, say

indicators.note: recycled means reused in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to stop playing the same old songs in stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges TIME and BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient music is low-key background sound such as is piped into shops.

clue.text: Emerging with a whiff of sodium?

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a whiff is a scent

explanation.surface: Something appearing, accompanied by a faint chemical smell.
explanation.walkthrough: A whiff of sodium is sodium's scent, so NA comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means coming into being, just beginning to develop.

clue.text: Sign points to sorceress's residence

indicators.note: to means the points are attached to the end of the residence

parts.note: the Witch of Endor is a biblical sorceress, consulted by King Saul
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A signpost directs travellers to a witch's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a cheque or document is to sign it on the back.
